name: Southeast Peak Standard (Home Lake approach)
approach: Drive Highway 101 to Sequim Bay State Park area, turn left on Louella Road for 1 mile, then left on Palo Alto Road for 1.1 miles to the Forest Boundary. Palo Alto becomes FS Road 28. Turn right onto FS Road 2880, drive past Dungeness Forks Campground for 1 mile, stay left onto FS Road 2870 for 8.7 miles to Upper Dungeness Trailhead. Upper Dungeness Trail is the shortest and easiest approach. Hike the trail 3.4 miles and 600 feet to Camp Handy, then take the left fork and continue 3 miles and 1,850 feet to Boulder Camp (total: 6.4 miles, 2,450 feet gain). From Boulder Camp, continue south approximately 1.5-2 miles, crossing creeks, until you reach the final larger creek that flows from the cirque SE of Warrior Peak. Continue past this creek to a boulder field, then head up and back left toward the creek, staying under a band of cliffs, and continue up the boulders approximately 1 mile and 1,200 feet to reach the cirque at approximately 5,900 feet.

approach_variants.name: Upper Dungeness Trail, Camp Handy and Boulder Shelter to the southeast cirque
approach_variants.notes:
From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park turn on Louella Road for a mile, then Palo Alto Road for 1.1 miles to the forest boundary, where Palo Alto becomes FS Road 28. Right on FS 2880 past Dungeness Forks Campground, then left on FS 2870 for 8.7 miles to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead. Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass required at the kiosk.

Trail #833.2 is the shortest and easiest approach. Hike 3.2-3.4 miles and about 600 ft to Camp Handy at roughly 3,100 ft, a riverfront meadow with a cedar-shingle shelter, then take the uphill fork and continue about 3 miles and 1,850 ft to Boulder Camp / Boulder Shelter at 6.3-6.4 miles and roughly 4,890-4,950 ft. The creek there is the most reliable water on the approach.

From Boulder Shelter hike south about 2 miles on the Dungeness / Constance Pass trail, crossing several creeks, toward Home Lake.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep. Snow in the summit couloir into early season is an improvement on the scree that replaces it
hazards: Loose, poor-quality rock on the final headwall above the 7,000 ft saddle — a recurring theme in every account
Rockfall in the couloir between the twin summits, worst with parties above or after freeze-thaw
Glissade and uncontrolled-slide risk descending the snow chute if the runout is not fully visible — one party described nearly going over a cliff band on nearby terrain
Faint use-trail-only route-finding above the trail through forest, meadow and talus
Fast-moving Pacific frontal systems and late-summer afternoon thunderstorms
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The first test is a creek you must not cross. Leave the trail before crossing the major stream that drains the Warrior / Inner Constance cirque. That stream is the last and largest of the several you meet going south from Boulder Shelter. Then climb east — steep forest, then steep open meadow, then talus — staying north of the streambed the whole way. The streambed is the handrail and it stays on your right. If you have crossed it and it is now on your left, you are on the wrong side of the drainage.

The arrival test is the cirque at about 5,900 ft, and it is unambiguous because it is a closed basin: the ground stops rising in front of you and the headwall closes round. From there, head north to the obvious couloir between the two peaks. Warrior has twin summits and the couloir runs up between them to a saddle at about 7,000 ft. There is one gully in that headwall with a summit on each side of it. If the gully you are in has a summit on only one side, it is not the one.

The test at the top of the couloir is which way to turn, and it is the single most useful sentence for this peak in fog: at the saddle, the higher peak is on your right. The southeast summit is the true top; the northwest summit at roughly 7,285 ft is the lower one. Coming up the couloir from the cirque, the true summit is to the right. Turn left and you will climb the wrong peak on ground just as loose.

Second test, on the summit block: above the saddle there is 20 to 50 feet of exposed, poor-quality rock rated Class 4 to low fifth on the block's northwest side, often gained over steep snow or a snow moat, and many parties fix a hand line on it. If your last obstacle before the top is a walk rather than a short difficult rock step, you are on the wrong summit.

What the season changes: the couloir is steep but straightforward when snow-filled, common early season; melted out it is a brutal scree slog to the same saddle. Both are the route.

approach_variants.name: Home Lake basecamp, from either the Dungeness or the Dosewallips side
approach_variants.notes:
Home Lake at about 5,308-5,330 ft, walled in by Mount Constance and Warrior Peak just below Constance Pass, is the standard basecamp for this climb and it is reachable from two directions: north up the Upper Dungeness / Constance Pass trail at roughly 9.3 miles from the Upper Dungeness Trailhead, or south from the Dosewallips road end over Constance Pass. An Olympic National Park wilderness permit is required.

Camping at Home Lake rather than pushing from Boulder Shelter turns this into a comfortable two-day trip and puts you a mile from the cirque. It is also the camp shared with Mount Fricaba, Mount Mystery and Mount Deception parties, so it is well-used ground with an established site.

From the lake, leave the basin and climb east into the Warrior / Inner Constance cirque through meadow and talus.
hazards: Same as the Boulder Shelter variant: loose summit rock, couloir rockfall, glissade runout, faint route-finding
Home Lake sits below Constance Pass, so an exit north regains meaningful height before the long descent
Wilderness permit required and the site is popular with parties climbing four different peaks
approach_variants.baseFinding: From Home Lake the test is the same streambed, worked from the other end: leave the lake basin heading east into the cirque, staying north of the stream that drains it. The stream is the handrail either way — approaching from Boulder Shelter you must not cross it, and approaching from the lake you must keep it below and to your right as you climb. The arrival test is the same closed cirque at about 5,900 ft, and then the obvious couloir between the two peaks running north to the saddle at about 7,000 ft — the one gully with a summit on each side of it. And the same turn at the top: at the saddle the higher, true summit is on your right (southeast). The 20 to 50 ft Class 4 / low fifth step on the block's northwest side is the last obstacle; if there is no step, you are on the northwest summit. Honest limit: this variant differs from the one above only in where you sleep and which direction you walk in. It is recorded separately because the route is titled for the Home Lake approach and a reader should not have to reconcile that with an approach description that starts from Boulder Shelter.

waypoints.name: Upper Dungeness Trailhead
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass required ($5/day, cashless payment only); trail #833.2 starts here into Buckhorn Wilderness.
waypoints.directions: From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Road and follow it for about a mile, then turn left onto Palo Alto Road for 1.1 miles to the national forest boundary, where the road becomes FS Road 28. Turn right onto FS Road 2880, pass Dungeness Forks Campground after about a mile, then stay left onto FS Road 2870 and follow it 8.7 miles to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required at the kiosk, paid at $5/day, cashless only.

waypoints.name: Camp Handy
waypoints.note: Riverfront meadow with a cedar-shingle shelter along the Dungeness River; popular first-night camp and last easy water before the climb steepens.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Upper Dungeness Trail #833.2 upstream along the Dungeness River, staying left at the Royal Basin Trail junction, about 3.4 miles and 600 ft of gain to Camp Handy.

waypoints.name: Boulder Shelter
waypoints.note: Shelter structure amid large boulders after a steep 1,800+ ft climb from Camp Handy; the creek here is the most reliable water source before Home Lake.
waypoints.directions: Just past Camp Handy take the uphill fork and climb steeply, with two creek crossings, about 3 miles and 1,850 ft to Boulder Shelter.

waypoints.name: Home Lake
waypoints.note: Small alpine lake walled in by Mt. Constance and Warrior Peak; standard base camp for the climb, sits just below Constance Pass. Olympic NP wilderness permit (Recreation.gov) required.
waypoints.directions: From Boulder Shelter take the Constance Pass trail south rather than the trail toward Marmot Pass, cross into Olympic National Park, and continue past several creek crossings to Home Lake below Constance Pass.

waypoints.name: Warrior/Inner Constance cirque entry
waypoints.note: Leave the Home Lake basin and climb east into the Warrior/Inner Constance cirque through meadow and talus, staying north of the streambed draining the cirque.
waypoints.directions: Leave the trail at Home Lake and climb east into the Warrior/Inner Constance cirque over meadow and talus to about 5,800 ft, where the headwall closes around the basin.

waypoints.name: Saddle couloir (rockfall/loose rock)
waypoints.note: Prominent north-northeast-trending couloir to the ~7,000 ft saddle between the twin summits; snow-filled and icy early season, a loose scree slog when melted out, with rockfall risk in the gully between the two peaks.
waypoints.directions: From the cirque head north into the obvious couloir that runs up between the twin summits, and climb it to the saddle at about 7,000 ft: snow early in the season, loose scree once it melts out. Watch for rockfall in the gully.

waypoints.name: Summit block rock step
waypoints.note: Above the saddle, 20-50 ft of exposed, poor-quality rock rated Class 4 to low 5th (5.2); many parties fix a hand line here for less-experienced climbers.
waypoints.directions: At the saddle turn right toward the higher southeast summit and cross to the foot of the summit block, where 20 to 50 ft of exposed, poor rock on its northwest side is the crux, often reached over steep snow or a moat.

waypoints.name: Warrior Peak (Southeast Summit)
waypoints.note: True summit is the southeast of the two tied peaks (~7,320 ft); Fred Beckey made the first ascent of both summits solo in 1945.
waypoints.directions: Climb the Class 4 to low 5th rock step, roped or on a fixed hand line if needed, and scramble the last short distance to the southeast summit.
